title: A Quick Way To Calm Your Class, Build Rapport, And End Bullying
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin recommends a single spoken statement teachers can deliver at the start of a day or period, promising students that any bullying, teasing, or discomfort will be addressed if reported through an email, note, or trusted friend. He describes the ripple effects: lowered classroom anxiety, greater trust in the teacher, and a subtle deterrent effect on would-be bullies who realize they can no longer act in the shadows. He ties the strategy to the Law of Reciprocity, arguing that students who feel protected respond with greater cooperation and effort. Crucially, he stresses the promise must be genuine and followed through on, since making the statement publicly obligates the teacher to act. He recommends repeating it about monthly, more often early in the year or when bullying signs appear.
points: Recommends a specific spoken promise—delivered to the whole class—that any bullying or discomfort will be addressed if reported.
Ties the strategy to the Law of Reciprocity: students who feel protected respond with greater trust and cooperation.
Notes the statement also puts potential bullies on notice that they can no longer act without consequence in the shadows.
Stresses that the promise must be genuine and consistently honored, since making it publicly creates real accountability.
Suggests repeating the statement about once a month, more frequently early in the year or when bullying signs emerge.
quotes: If you’re ever bullied, bothered, or made fun of, or feel uncomfortable in this classroom in any way, I promise to fix it. You can send me an email, slip me a note, or ask to speak with me privately.
Rest assured, I’ll move mountains to take care of the problem so you can feel safe to learn and enjoy being in this class.
When you extend kindness to your students, and boldly promise their protection from the scourge of bullying, or any other impediment to learning, they’ll want to pay you back in spades.
The statement, you see, puts you on notice. It exerts a soft pressure to fulfill your promises. Thus, you must follow through.
The statement also puts bullies on notice that if they do engage in hurtful behavior, there will be heck to pay.
That they can count on you to be a leader they can trust. Maybe the only one they’ve ever known.
